steps.title: Console before sign-in
steps.note: The single-page console is served by the Spring Boot application itself (no separate frontend server). Every API call the page makes is listed in the panel at the bottom.
steps.caption: Open the console. Users: engineer, approver, admin (role-based access)

steps.title: Signed in as engineer, dashboard
steps.note: GET /api/v1/whoami identifies the user and roles; the dashboard reads GET /api/v1/metrics/summary. The database is fresh, so all counters start at zero.
steps.caption: Sign in as engineer

steps.title: Create form
steps.note: Original URL, optional custom alias and optional expiration date.
steps.caption: URL shortener: create a short link with a custom alias

steps.title: Short URL created
steps.note: POST /api/v1/urls returned 201; GET /api/v1/urls refreshed the table.
steps.caption: URL shortener: create a short link with a custom alias

steps.title: Three redirects recorded
steps.note: GET /api/v1/urls/{code} answers 302 (the browser reports it as an opaque redirect). Click count and timestamps are persisted.
steps.caption: Simulate three visits: each is an HTTP 302 redirect and counts a click

steps.title: Analytics
steps.note: GET /api/v1/urls/{code}/analytics: total clicks, first and last access timestamps, referrer statistics and daily click statistics.
steps.caption: Analytics: total clicks, first/last access, referrers, daily clicks

steps.title: Deactivated link answers 410
steps.note: DELETE /api/v1/urls/{code} returned 204 (soft delete); visiting the link now returns 410 Gone.
steps.caption: Deactivate (soft delete): the link now answers 410 Gone

steps.title: Link reactivated
steps.note: PUT /api/v1/urls/{code}/status {active:true} reactivated the link.
steps.caption: Deactivate (soft delete): the link now answers 410 Gone

steps.title: Workflow created
steps.note: POST /api/v1/workflows created the workflow with 13 DAG nodes (nothing has run yet). Dashed nodes are human approval gates.
steps.caption: Scenario 1 (greenfield): requirement to workflow

steps.title: Executed, waiting for final approval
steps.note: POST /execute ran requirement, planning, architecture, then implementation and test-planning in parallel, documentation and validation, security review. The workflow paused at the human final approval; the two conditional gates were skipped.
steps.caption: Execute: agents run as a DAG, independent branches run in parallel

steps.title: Engineer approval denied (403)
steps.note: The server answered 403 and explains which role is needed. Approvals are enforced by role (APPROVER).
steps.caption: Governance: an engineer is NOT allowed to approve

steps.title: Approved, workflow completed
steps.note: POST /approve by the approver granted the gate; the workflow resumed and COMPLETED (release readiness and engineering summary).
steps.caption: Sign in as approver and approve the release

steps.title: Generated artifacts
steps.note: GET /artifacts?includeContent=true: versioned artifacts, all ACCEPTED after final approval; content stored in the approved workspace only.
steps.caption: Sign in as approver and approve the release

steps.title: Decision lineage
steps.note: GET /decisions: each decision lists the upstream decisions it builds on (Builds on column).
steps.caption: Sign in as approver and approve the release

steps.title: Audit trail
steps.note: GET /api/v1/audit/workflows/{id}: every sensitive step is recorded (creation, task results, approvals, artifact promotion).
steps.caption: Sign in as approver and approve the release

steps.title: Workflow metrics
steps.note: GET /api/v1/metrics/workflows/{id}: latency, agent executions, retries, approval wait.
steps.caption: Sign in as approver and approve the release

steps.title: Engineering summary
steps.note: GET /summary: final engineering summary and release readiness. The platform never deploys; it only assesses readiness.
steps.caption: Sign in as approver and approve the release

steps.title: Brownfield workflow executed
steps.note: Same DAG, different content. The architecture stage first scans the real URL shortener module of this application by reflection.
steps.caption: Scenario 2 (brownfield): enhance the existing URL shortener

steps.title: Change impact analysis
steps.note: Architecture output: impacted APIs, entities, services and repositories discovered from the actual module, existing test discovery and backward-compatibility assessment.
steps.caption: Change impact analysis built from the real code base

steps.title: Regression risks
steps.note: Regression risks and the statement that the change is backward compatible.
steps.caption: Change impact analysis built from the real code base

steps.title: Brownfield completed
steps.note: Approved and completed.
steps.caption: Change impact analysis built from the real code base

steps.title: Paused for assumption approval
steps.note: Blocking ambiguities were found. Planning has NOT started; the workflow waits for a human to approve the provisional assumptions.
steps.caption: Scenario 3: an ambiguous requirement must not become silent decisions

steps.title: Questions and assumptions
steps.note: Requirements output: clarification questions, provisional assumptions (for example p95 latency and availability targets) and missing information such as baselines.
steps.caption: Clarification questions, provisional assumptions and missing information

steps.title: Second gate: high-impact design
steps.note: After the assumptions were approved the plan was produced. Introducing a shared cache is a high-impact architecture change, so a second approval is required. test-planning already completed in parallel.
steps.caption: Approval 1 of 3: material assumptions

steps.title: Third gate: release
steps.note: Design approved; implementation, documentation, validation and review ran; final release approval pending.
steps.caption: Approval 2 of 3: design

steps.title: Ambiguous scenario completed
steps.note: Completed after three human approvals. Release readiness is READY_WITH_CONDITIONS because the targets are still provisional.
steps.caption: Approval 3 of 3: release

steps.title: Rejected, rolled back
steps.note: POST /reject: the workflow is ROLLED_BACK and its staged artifact versions are reverted (a safe, reversible operation).
steps.caption: Rejection: a rejected approval rolls the workflow back

steps.title: Artifacts reverted
steps.note: All artifacts are REVERTED; nothing was accepted.
steps.caption: Rejection: a rejected approval rolls the workflow back

steps.title: Design approval for a sensitive change
steps.note: The architecture marks a SECURITY_SENSITIVE_CHANGE, which needs a human approval before implementation.
steps.caption: Security: a request to disable authentication

steps.title: Safe-stopped on a critical finding
steps.note: The review stage found a critical security finding and the workflow stopped (SAFE_STOPPED, SECURITY_CONCERN). The reason is persisted; nothing downstream ran.
steps.caption: Critical review finding: the workflow SAFE-STOPS

steps.title: Engineer cannot resume (403)
steps.note: Resuming a safe-stopped workflow requires the APPROVER role and an acknowledgement.
steps.caption: Only an approver may resume, with an acknowledgement

steps.title: Approver resumes: stopped again
steps.note: The approver resumed with an acknowledgement; the same policy violation stops it again, proving the guard cannot be bypassed.
steps.caption: Only an approver may resume, with an acknowledgement

steps.title: Fault injection denied for engineer
steps.note: POST /api/v1/admin/fault-injection returned 403; the message names the required ADMIN role.
steps.caption: Admin area: engineer is not allowed to inject faults

steps.title: Fault rule injected
steps.note: The next two DECOMPOSE_TASKS calls will fail with a timeout.
steps.caption: Admin: make the next 2 task-planning LLM calls time out

steps.title: Planning needed 3 attempts
steps.note: The planning task shows Attempts = 3: two transient failures were retried and the third attempt succeeded.
steps.caption: The workflow retries with exponential backoff (200 ms, 400 ms)

steps.title: Retry audit events
steps.note: TASK_RETRY_SCHEDULED events record each attempt and the backoff (200 ms, then 400 ms).
steps.caption: The workflow retries with exponential backoff (200 ms, 400 ms)

steps.title: Low-impact replan applied
steps.note: POST /replan: only documentation and everything downstream are marked for re-execution; completed upstream work is preserved. No approval is needed for a low-impact change.
steps.caption: Replanning: documentation changed

steps.title: Only stale tasks re-ran
steps.note: The workflow re-ran just the affected tasks (revision 2) and paused again at the final approval.
steps.caption: Replanning: documentation changed

steps.title: High-impact replan waits for approval
steps.note: Nothing changes until a human approves the proposal; the exact impact (impacted and preserved tasks) is shown for review.
steps.caption: High-impact architecture change needs approval

steps.title: Replan approved, decisions superseded
steps.note: After approval the architecture and its dependants re-ran. Earlier decisions are struck through (superseded) but kept for traceability, never silently overwritten.
steps.caption: High-impact architecture change needs approval

steps.title: Revisions after replan
steps.note: architecture now shows revision 2 while requirements and planning remain revision 1 (preserved).
steps.caption: High-impact architecture change needs approval

steps.title: Metrics dashboard
steps.note: GET /api/v1/metrics/summary: success and failure rate, retries, rollbacks, safe-stops, end-to-end latency, approval wait, task success rate and MTTR, all derived from stored data.
steps.caption: Metrics computed from the persisted workflow history

steps.section: Run all flows from the browser
steps.title: Run all flows: ready
steps.note: One button executes every API flow with the engineer, approver and admin users.
steps.caption: Run every API flow from the browser (about 1 minute)

steps.section: Run all flows from the browser
steps.title: Run all flows: in progress
steps.note: Progress bar and live results while the flows execute.
steps.caption: Running all flows ...

steps.section: Run all flows from the browser
steps.title: Run all flows: result summary
steps.note: Every check passed. The page made all of these API calls itself.
steps.caption: Result of the full API run

steps.section: Run all flows from the browser
steps.title: Run all flows: complete list of checks
steps.note: Full list of checks (full-page capture).
steps.caption: Result of the full API run
